The blue star sits alone at the far end of a bare two-point stub with no neutrino-candidate charge anywhere near it. Measured from state.json segments: the only segments touching the main vertex (-56.6,133.3,253.2) at 0.00 cm are 62028 (cluster 62, pdg 13, 35.3 cm) and 62037 (cluster 62, pdg 211, 3.4 cm) - and cluster 62 is NOT one of the three clusters carrying the reconstruction (the cloud div says 'ids 17, 22, 23'). The nearest neutrino-candidate charge is 48.5 cm away (22013, the shower's own member) and the 168 cm track 17000 is 124.4 cm away. On ov-iso the event is two long, roughly parallel, never-touching tracks - 22014 (123.1 cm, cluster 22, grey/unowned) carrying the shower 22018 at its top end, and 17000 (168.0 cm, cluster 17) far to the right - with the star floating above and between them on a third cluster. Nothing converges at the star, so the vertex is placed off the neutrino candidate entirely. Two observations recorded but NOT acted on, because the vertex verdict pre-empts them: (a) 22014, a 123.1 cm pdg-13 track in the SAME cluster 22, sits at 14.2 cm / 6.0 deg, tier 1, from shower 22018's axis and is UNOWNED - this is the reverse of the usual grey case: swallowing a 123 cm MIP stem into a 108.6 MeV shower would be over-clustering, and the reconstruction's from_vertices walk_exclude looks right to me; I did NOT mark it. (b) 22018 reaches out to two 0.25-0.27 cm fragments 64030 (73.4 cm / 6.8 deg) and 65031 (87.4 cm / 10.9 deg, tier 2) via pass4_angle, a long reach for a shower whose own length is 36.9 cm, but the charge is negligible.
